welcome.label: Welcome · the melted box

parts.label: ❓ The question
parts.title: Is the art show over?
parts.body: One box. One melted slab. One claim to settle.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a crayon and press it between your hands.) What if this ended up as a puddle? Would it still be a crayon? Would it still be wax?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
Three hundred crayons were shipped here for the art show. The truck sat in the sun, and the box arrived as one solid rainbow slab. The freight company says the wax became a new material, so they owe the school nothing.

[ON SCREEN: The question]
Are they right? Find four clues today and you can settle this claim yourself.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · the sealed bag (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🔒 Sealed
parts.title: Nothing in, nothing out
parts.body: So anything that changes is still in there.

warmup.script:
(Hold up a zip bag, seal it, and shake it.) Nothing gets in. Nothing gets out.

[ON SCREEN: The bag]
Drag the bag onto the scale and read the number. Then press Wait an hour. The ice melts into water.

[ON SCREEN: Sealed]
Here is the part I want you to do before you peek: call the number. Will the scale say less, more, or exactly the same? Pick first, then find out. That is Clue one.

part1.label: Part 1 · call the number first (Clue 2)

parts.label: 🔢 Three calls
parts.title: Type your number before you weigh

part1.script:
(Write a number on your hand and cover it.) Scientists write down what they expect BEFORE they measure. That way they can’t fool themselves later.

[ON SCREEN: Three calls]
Read the starting number, make the change, then type your call and weigh it. Three changes. Watch what the number does every single time.

part2.label: Part 2 · the UNDO button (Clue 3)
part2.script:
(Mime pressing an undo key, then shrug.) Some things undo. Some things really don’t.

[ON SCREEN: Six undo buttons]
Press UNDO on all six and watch what happens. Then stamp each card: came back, or stuck that way.

[ON SCREEN: Same material]
Here is the part most people get wrong. Look at the material line under every card. Shredded paper is still paper. Broken glass is still glass. Hard to undo does not mean a new material.

part3.label: Part 3 · where did the water go?
part3.script:
[ON SCREEN: What the sun left]
These were ponds of seawater. The sun turned the water into vapor and it floated off into the air. The salt could not float off, so it stayed, every grain of it. Drag the slider on the photo and watch it happen. Nothing disappeared.

explore.label: Part 4 · the state dial (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🖍️ The wow
parts.title: One giant crayon
parts.body: The slab the company called ruined.

explore.script:
(Shiver, then fan yourself.) Cold enough and water is a solid. Hot enough and it is a gas.

[ON SCREEN: The dial]
Take the dial all the way up to the stovetop, then all the way back down to the freezer. Watch two readouts the whole time: the mass, and the material.

[ON SCREEN: The wow]
Then stay for the last bit. Dr. Nair takes that melted slab to the art room, and what comes out of the mold is worth seeing.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Was the claim fair?
parts.body: Four clues, and the form’s own two weights.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Use your four clues to settle the claim. Then stamp the form yourself, with your own two pieces of evidence on it.

[ON SCREEN: Your work]
Next, two short answers. For Part C, find four physical changes at home, sort them into ones you can undo and ones you can’t, and name the material that stays the same in each. Then sketch and label two of them. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Any change you can’t undo must be a chemical change.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Tear a piece of paper in half.) I can’t undo that. Does that make it a chemical change?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says any change you can’t undo must be chemical. Think about the shredded paper, and think about that rainbow slab.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain in your own words how they prove your claim. Try starting with: This shows that.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🖍️ Your specimen
parts.title: A sliver of the rainbow crayon
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next lesson
parts.title: Chemical changes
parts.body: The last lesson of the year.

closing.script:
(Hold up a crayon and wave it.) The art show is on.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and a sliver of that giant rainbow crayon goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next lesson]
One lesson left in the whole year, and it is the big one. Tomorrow the material really does become something new.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
